chemistry-killer-07.title: Mole
chemistry-killer-07.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
chemistry-killer-07.material: Na état standard (STP, 0 °C, 1 atm; 1 mol tî gaz = 22.4 L), mélange tî gaz so asara na méthane ($\mathrm{CH_4}$) na dioxyde tî carbone ($\mathrm{CO_2}$) ayeke volume 11.2 L na masse 16.4 g. Masse atomique ayeke H=1, C=12, O=16 na nombre tî Avogadro ayeke $N_A$. Nombre tî atome kûê so ayeke na yâ mélange tî gaz so ayeke nyen?
chemistry-killer-07.s.s1.prompt: Na état standard (STP, 0 °C, 1 atm; 1 mol tî gaz = 22.4 L), mélange tî gaz so asara na méthane ($\mathrm{CH_4}$) na dioxyde tî carbone ($\mathrm{CO_2}$) ayeke volume 11.2 L na masse 16.4 g. Masse atomique ayeke H=1, C=12, O=16 na nombre tî Avogadro ayeke $N_A$. Nombre tî atome kûê so ayeke na yâ mélange tî gaz so ayeke nyen?
chemistry-killer-07.s.s1.explain:
Étape 1: Nombre total tî mole = 11.2 L ÷ 22.4 L/mol = 0.5 mol → x + y = 0.5.
Étape 2: Masse: 16x + 44y = 16.4. A zia y = 0.5 − x: 16x + 22 − 44x = 16.4 → 28x = 5.6 → x = 0.2, y = 0.3.
Étape 3: Nombre tî atome: $\mathrm{CH_4}$ ayeke atome 5 na molécule oko → 0.2 × 5 = 1.0 mol, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ ayeke atome 3 na molécule oko → 0.3 × 3 = 0.9 mol. Somme 1.9 mol atome = $1.9\,N_A$.
Réponse: $1.9\,N_A$ (c). (Réponse fausse: 1.5 ayeke tongana a bâ kûê ayeke CO2, 2.5 ayeke tongana a bâ kûê ayeke CH4, 1.7 ayeke valeur so a compter atome tî CH4 ge H 4)
chemistry-killer-07.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
chemistry-killer-07.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
